summary: Jules Oppert worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn under Christian Lassen and Georg Freytag, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Kiel (PhD). He held professorships at INALCO, the Bibliothèque nationale de France, and the Collège de France.

Jules Pierre Barthoux worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing a Dr.-ès-sciences at the University of Lille by 1922, he was in charge of the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan from 1923 to 1933.
Jules Thonnelier was a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. He held memberships in the Société Asiatique and the Société de l'histoire de France.

Julia A. B. Hegewald specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at SOAS University of London (BA, PhD), the University of Oxford (MA), and RWTH Aachen University (Habilitation), later holding a post at Heidelberg University from circa 2005 to 2010.

Julia Ching was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University, taught at Columbia and Yale, and became a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

Julia König specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Jena from 2006 to 2013, earning a Magister Artium, and held a post there in the Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences from 2008 to 2009.

Julia Leslie worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sussex and the University of Oxford (M.Phil.). She taught at Harvard University and served at SOAS University of London as Lecturer and Reader in Hindu Studies from 1990 to 2004.

Julia Shaw works in archaeology, history, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Her attested academic posts include positions at the University of York in 1997, University College London in 2016, the University of Warsaw in 2017, and the University of Alberta in 2018.
Julian Schott is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. As of 2026, he is attested as faculty at the University of Vienna and a research fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Juliane Schober specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign by 1989, she served as an associate professor of religious studies at Arizona State University, attested in 1997 and 2007.

Julie Gifford specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds and held an attested post at Miami University in 2011.

Julien Girard de Rialle worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and under Honoré-Joseph Chavée, later serving as a lecturer at the Sorbonne.

Julien Levesque specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a PhD from EHESS after degrees from Sciences Po and Columbia. He has held positions at EHESS, INALCO, CSH, Ashoka University, the University of Zurich, and CNRS.

Julien Vinson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Nationale du Génie Rural, des Eaux et des Forêts. From 1879 to 1921, he served as professor of Hindustani and Tamil at INALCO.

Julieta Rotaru works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Bucharest (BA, PhD) and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (MA). Her posts include the University of Bucharest (2000–2015), Södertörn University (2017–2021), and INALCO (2021).

Julius Dutoit was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Universities of Munich, Giessen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD), as well as under Ernst Kuhn and Adalbert Kuhn. From 1929 to 1934, he was director of Riemenschneider-Gymnasium.

Julius Eggeling specialized in Indology. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and later Theodor Aufrecht. He served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and was a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier. He served as a librarian in Tübingen, director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire, and professor at the University of Strasbourg.
Julius Evola worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at ITI L.Da Vinci and the Sapienza University of Rome (circa 1916–1918), and held a post at the Ahnenerbe from 1943 to 1945.
